title: Post-fire structural and utility hazards
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and salvage after a fire or smoke event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a fire-damaged building, release it, or certify it as safe.
learningOutcomes: Recognise structural and utility hazards after a fire and stop work until qualified parties resolve them.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how to recognise structural and utility hazards after a fire, and how to stop work and refer them. It does not authorise entry, isolation, reconnection or repair of any structure or utility. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Post-fire structural and utility hazards
instruction.body: A room may look stable while a damaged electrical distribution board or a sagging ceiling is visible in photographs. Use non-intrusive visual observation only. Treat damaged wiring, gas lines, overhead loads, weakened stairs and unstable walls as stop-work hazards. Qualified utility and structural personnel decide on isolation and entry permissions, and no entry is made until competent parties have resolved these hazards. In training, mark unsafe entry routes on a mock floor plan and produce a referral request. Do not propose do-it-yourself electrical or structural work.

procedure: Stop work and stay out of any area where structural or utility hazards are not resolved.
Record visible damage by non-intrusive observation and dated photographs only.
Mark unsafe entry routes, overhead loads and damaged utilities on a floor plan or hazard map.
Do not operate, reset, test or repair damaged electrical or gas equipment.
Refer utility isolation to the responsible utility and structural assessment to a qualified person, in writing.
Record the referral, the person referred to and the no-entry conditions, and wait for written confirmation before any entry.

workedExamples.situation: A room looks stable, but photographs show a damaged electrical distribution board and a sagging ceiling.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Damaged utilities and a sagging ceiling are stop-work hazards. Entry waits until qualified utility and structural personnel have resolved them, and no do-it-yourself repair is attempted.

workedExamples.situation: A worker wants to reset a tripped breaker in a fire-damaged room so the work area has light.
workedExamples.reasoning: Refuse. Do not operate damaged electrical equipment. Refer the request to the responsible utility or a licensed electrician, and record it.

equipmentAndPpe: No PPE makes a damaged structure or utility safe to enter. The qualified party decides on entry.
Hazard marking, barrier tape and no-entry signage agreed with the site controller.

commonErrors.error: Entering a room that looks stable despite visible damage to electrical or structural elements.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat visible damage as a stop-work hazard and refer to qualified personnel.

commonErrors.error: Resetting a breaker or switching on equipment to light the work area.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not operate damaged equipment. Request power or lighting through the responsible party.

commonErrors.error: Treating a photograph as proof that a structure is sound.
commonErrors.prevention: Photographs record conditions. They do not establish structural safety.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Isolating, re-energising or repairing damaged electrical and gas installations is restricted to licensed or authorised people. Completing this lesson does not authorise that work.
Western Australian guidance advises not entering a property until authorities confirm it is safe.
The rules for structural assessment and utility isolation vary by state and territory. Check the rule that applies to the site before any entry.

qualityStandard: The learner identifies damaged wiring, gas lines, overhead loads, weakened stairs and unstable walls as stop-work hazards.
The learner refuses to operate damaged equipment and does not propose do-it-yourself electrical or structural work.
documentationEvidence: Hazard and zoning worksheet with structural and utility observations, photographs and no-entry conditions.
Referral records to the utility and to the structural assessor, with dates and written confirmation.
summary: Visible damage to structures and utilities is a stop-work hazard.
Do not operate damaged electrical or gas equipment. Refer to qualified personnel.
Photographs record conditions. They do not clear a structure.

knowledgeChecks.question: A room looks stable, but photographs show a damaged electrical distribution board and a sagging ceiling. Is entry permitted?
options: Yes, if the room looks stable and the ceiling has no obvious sign of movement or damage
Yes, if the worker does a quick repair first to make the board safe to use for the job
No. Stop work until qualified utility and structural personnel have resolved the hazards.

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker wants to reset a tripped breaker in a fire-damaged room so the work area has light. What is correct?
options: Reset it if the breaker is labelled
No. Do not operate damaged electrical equipment. Refer the request to the responsible utility or a licensed electrician.

officialReferences.title: Asbestos safety after an emergency or disaster
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. Do not enter a property until authorities confirm it is safe. Avoid spreading ash or moving debris by sweeping or vacuuming. Never use high-pressure sprays; dampen ash and debris lightly to limit dust. Wear a P2 face mask and protective clothing such as sturdy boots and gloves, even if unsure whether asbestos is present. Contact a competent person or licensed asbestos assessor before clean-up starts. If asbestos is confirmed, a licensed asbestos removalist carries out the clean-up. Urgent removal: notify WorkSafe and submit the notification within 24 hours. Emergency work still requires a clearance. WA guidance only.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: Fire-scene release, structural and utility isolation, asbestos assessment and removal, and some waste handling are restricted to competent and, where the law requires, licensed people, and may be controlled by fire investigators, the police, structural engineers, utilities or the building owner. Insurer and owner permission do not replace a release from the authority that controls the site. Where that authority is not identified, do not proceed.

stopWorkAndReferral: Stop and refer when the structure or utilities are unresolved.
A stop-work decision is correct, so record it and restart only once the competent party confirms the scope in writing.
